newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. approves EgyptAir flights for Libyan pilgrims.
newsitem.headline: U.N. approves EgyptAir flights for Libyan pilgrims.

text.p: A U.N. sanctions committee said on Thursday it had given permission for an Egyptian airline, EgyptAir, to make 45 return flights between Libya and Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, with Libyans making the annual pilgrimage to Mecca.
The committee approved a similar arrangement last year.

Libya has been under U.N. sanctions since 1992, including a ban on international flights, for failing to hand over two men indicted by the United States and Britain in the bombing of a Pan Am airliner over Lockerbie, Scotland, in 1988, killing 270 people.
EgyptAir is permitted to operate 45 flights from Cairo to Tripoli and Beghazi, in Libya, to pick up pilgrims and fly them to Jeddah, and later fly them home.
U.N. officials will be involved in inspecting both the inbound and outbound flights in all four cities.
Egypt is required to provide the sanctions committee with advance notice of the flight schedules, routing and aircraft registration numbers.
All flights must be nonstop between the authorised destinations and none of the planes used may be owned by or leased from Libya, which is not to gain financially from the flights.

The sanctions against Libya, in addition to an air embargo, include a ban on arms sales and the downgrading of diplomatic relations with the North African country. They were toughened in 1993 with the addition of a freeze on some of Libya's assets abroad and a ban on its import of certain types of equipment used at oil terminals and refineries.
The Security Council reviews the sanctions every 120 days -- most recently March 14 -- but they have remained unchanged.

Libya has occasionally violated the sanctions. The last occasion was in January when a Libyan plane, without U.N. permission, flew an official delegation to Accra, Ghana. The sanctions committee has asked Libya for an explanation.
